themes.label: Introduction: one-shot vs. sequential structural-change tests
themes.need: Someone wanting real-time detection of structural change, not just one-shot retrospective testing, needs the motivation for a genuine sequential testing approach - why one-shot tests fail when repeatedly applied - and the paper's CUSUM and fluctuation (FL) monitoring proposals building on Wald's SPRT and sequential tests of power one.

themes.label: Why repeated retrospective tests fail; the boundary-crossing relation
themes.need: Someone tempted to monitor stability by repeatedly re-running a retrospective F or fluctuation test needs the demonstration that this inflates type-I error to one asymptotically (by the law of iterated logarithm), and the Robbins-Siegmund boundary-crossing relation (eq. 1) that instead controls asymptotic size via a properly chosen stopping boundary.

themes.label: Regression stability setup and the CUSUM/alternative detectors
themes.need: Someone wanting to monitor a linear regression model for post-sample instability needs the noncontamination assumption and the definition of a monitoring scheme (detector plus threshold), the CUSUM-of-recursive-residuals detector (eq. 2), its relation to other CUSUM/LR detectors in the engineering literature, and a preview of the fluctuation (FL) monitoring alternative.

themes.label: FCLT invariance principle and regular boundary functions
themes.need: Someone wanting to justify a monitoring boundary theoretically needs the FCLT setup and the abstract 'regular' boundary-function conditions (eq. 5-6) under which the Robbins-Siegmund-type limiting relation holds for general (non-iid) stochastic sequences satisfying an FCLT.

themes.label: Regularity lemmas and boundary-crossing theorems
themes.need: Someone wanting concrete, verifiable conditions on a boundary function needs Lemmas 3.1-3.2 (sufficient conditions for regularity, in terms of cadlag functions with countably many infinite-derivative points) and Theorems 3.3-3.4 establishing convergence of the boundary-crossing time and giving two closed-form boundary functions (eq. 7-8) with known crossing probabilities.

themes.label: CUSUM monitoring application
themes.need: Someone wanting to implement CUSUM monitoring of a regression for post-sample stability needs Corollary 3.5's asymptotic size formulas (eq. 9-10) under the two proposed boundary functions, the corresponding critical constants for 5%/10% size, and the consistency argument under a one-time parameter shift alternative.

themes.label: Fluctuation (FL) detector definition and multivariate FCLT
themes.need: Someone wanting to monitor stability via the fluctuation of sequential parameter estimates rather than residuals needs the FL detector definition (eq. 11-12), the multivariate FCLT condition it relies on, and the derivation that its limiting process is a k-dimensional Brownian bridge.

themes.label: Brownian-bridge crossing probability for FL monitoring
themes.need: Someone wanting a closed-form asymptotic size for FL monitoring needs the time-rescaling argument that reduces the Brownian-bridge crossing probability to a Wiener-process crossing probability (eq. 13), yielding the specific boundary function and its associated 5%/10% critical constants.

themes.label: FL monitoring power and consistency
themes.need: Someone wanting formal guarantees for FL monitoring needs Corollary 3.6's full statement (regularity conditions, the Brownian-bridge limit, and the k-dimensional asymptotic size formula) and Theorem 3.7's result that FL monitoring has asymptotic power one under a one-time parameter shift.

themes.label: Univariate location-model case and choice of window m
themes.need: Someone specializing FL monitoring to the simplest univariate mean-shift case needs the resulting closed-form boundary (eq. 14) and the discussion of how the choice of historical sample size m trades off finite-sample size accuracy against detection speed depending on where the break occurs.

themes.label: Relation to Wald's SPRT and the partially sequential two-sample test
themes.need: Someone wanting to relate FL monitoring to classical sequential testing theory needs the derivation that FL monitoring with beta0 known reduces to Wald's SPRT (with its known optimality only in the simple-vs-simple case), and the characterization of FL monitoring with beta0 unknown as a 'partially sequential two-sample test' related to but distinct from Switzer's procedure.

themes.label: Simulation design for FL monitoring's empirical size
themes.need: Someone wanting to replicate the finite-sample size simulation for FL monitoring needs the iid N(2,1) data-generating design, the range of historical sample sizes m and monitoring horizons q used, and the theoretical asymptotic size targets (5%/10%) being checked.

themes.label: Empirical size and first-hitting-time results (Tables I-II)
themes.need: Someone wanting the finite-sample size and detection-delay performance of FL monitoring needs Table I's empirical crossing probabilities across m and monitoring horizons, and Table II's empirical first-hitting-time distribution (mean, SD) under a simulated structural break.

themes.label: ARL/MRL interpretation and break-point estimation (Table III)
themes.need: Someone wanting to interpret FL monitoring's detection-delay behavior and locate a detected break needs the ARL/MRL discussion (including how detection speed depends on break location and window growth), and Table III's evaluation of using the maximum-LR-statistic point as a break-date estimator.

themes.label: Concluding remarks
themes.need: Someone wanting a compact summary of the paper's contribution needs the concluding recap of the CUSUM and FL monitoring procedures, the widened class of admissible boundary functions, and the open question of optimal boundary choice.

themes.label: Appendix: Theorem A (Robbins-Siegmund boundary crossing)
themes.need: Someone wanting the general machinery used to compute boundary-crossing probabilities for an arbitrary boundary needs Theorem A (Robbins and Siegmund), which expresses the crossing probability in terms of an exponential-martingale transform and a measure F, from which the paper's specific boundaries (7)-(8) are derived as special cases.

themes.label: Proofs of Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.3, Corollary 3.6, Theorem 3.7
themes.need: Someone wanting to verify the paper's formal results needs the complete proofs of Lemma 3.1 (regularity of cadlag boundary functions), Theorem 3.3 (convergence via the continuous mapping theorem), Corollary 3.6 (the FL monitoring size formula), and Theorem 3.7 (FL monitoring's asymptotic power one).
